'''Keith Damon Appling''' (born February 13, 1992) is an American former [[basketball]] player and convicted murderer. After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Appling appeared sporadically for the [[Orlando Magic]] before being waived in 2016. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State University]].

==Early life==
Appling played high school basketball at [[Pershing High School]] in Detroit. In 2009, as a junior, he led his team to win the [[Michigan High School Athletic Association]] Class A Basketball Championship.<ref>{{cite news|title=2009 MHSAA Boys Basketball Finals|url=http://www.mhsaa.com/MHSAA_ARCHIVE/sports/bbb/09final.html|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=MHSAA.com|archive-date=February 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160213061644/http://www.mhsaa.com/MHSAA_ARCHIVE/sports/bbb/09final.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the title game, he set a MHSAA Championship Game record by scoring 49 points,<ref>{{cite news|title=MHSAA Record Book|url=http://www.mhsaa.com/sports/boys-basketball/record-book/finals-records|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=MHSAA.com|archive-date=October 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021041749/http://www.mhsaa.com/sports/boys-basketball/record-book/finals-records|url-status=dead}}</ref> beating the previous record of 47 established by [[Antoine Joubert]] in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Final Round Records |url=https://www.mhsaa.com/Sports/Boys-Basketball/Record-Book/Final-Round-Records |access-date=April 23, 2020 |website=MHSAA.com |archive-date=October 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020115746/https://www.mhsaa.com/Sports/Boys-Basketball/Record-Book/Final-Round-Records |url-status=dead }}</ref> The next year, as a senior, he was the [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] award winner.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rezler |first=Rich |date=March 22, 2010 |title=Detroit Pershing's Keith Appling wins Mr. Basketball |url=https://www.annarbor.com/sports/high-school/detroit-pershings-keith-appling-wins-mr-basketball |access-date=January 8, 2024 |work=annarbor.com}}</ref> At the end of his high school career, he was considered a high-level recruit and was the 34th-ranked player using the RSCI (Recruiting Services Consensus Index) rankings. In his senior campaign, Appling averaged 28 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists.<ref>{{cite news |date=March 22, 2010 |title=Keith Appling wins lopsided Mr. Basketball vote |url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2010/03/keith_appling_wins_lopsided_mr.html |access-date=January 8, 2024 |work=MLive.com}}</ref> He was selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during which he scored 10 points.

==College career==
As a freshman at MSU, Appling averaged 6.4 points and 2.8 rebounds per game while shooting over 41% from three-point range. In his sophomore year, he averaged 11.6 points, 2.9 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. He earned All-[[Big Ten]] third-team honors while leading the Spartans to the Big Ten regular-season and tournament championship. In his junior year, he started every game and led the Spartans in scoring with 13.4 points a game and assists with 3.3 per game while earning All-Big Ten second-team honors. In his senior year, he averaged 11.2 points, 3.0 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite news|title=Keith Appling Bio|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/appling_keith00.html|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=MSUSpartans.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304012932/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/appling_keith00.html|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Keith Appling Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/keith-appling-1.html|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Appling joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On September 23, 2014, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{cite news |date=September 23, 2014 |title=Lakers Sign Four to Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140923four_signed_trainingcamp |access-date=September 25, 2015 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> but was later waived on October 20.<ref>{{cite news |date=October 20, 2014 |title=Lakers Waive Appling and Tyler |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/141020lakers_wavie_appling_tyler |access-date=September 25, 2015 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 1, he was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] as an affiliate player of the Lakers.<ref>{{cite news|title=D-Fenders Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/141101_finalize_tc_roster/|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2014|archive-date=January 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125213434/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/141101_finalize_tc_roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 7, 2015, he was traded to the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] in exchange for the returning player rights to Cleveland Melvin.<ref>{{cite news|title=BayHawks Trade for Appling|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4935124|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 7, 2015}}</ref> In 38 D-League games in 2014–15 (28 for Los Angeles, 10 for Erie), Appling averaged 10.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.9 assists in 24.4 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Keith Appling D-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/a/applike01d.html|access-date=January 19, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

In July 2015, Appling joined the [[Orlando Magic]] white team for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=June 30, 2015 |title=Orlando Magic Announce Rosters for Southwest Airlines Orlando Pro Summer League |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-announce-rosters-southwest-airlines-orlando-pro-summer-league |access-date=September 25, 2015 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On September 24, he signed with the Magic,<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=September 24, 2015 |title=Magic Sign Four Free Agents To Round Out Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-four-free-agents-round-out-training-camp-roster |access-date=September 24, 2015 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> but was later waived by the team on October 19 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=October 19, 2015 |title=Magic Waive Appling and Sibert |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-appling-and-sibert |access-date=October 19, 2015 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 31, he was reacquired by the Erie BayHawks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Erie BayHawks Announce Affiliate, Returning Players|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065433|access-date=October 31, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> On |work=NBA.com}}</ref> That same day, he was named in the East All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite expired, he was reacquired by the BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA D-League Transactions |url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |access-date=February 8, 2016 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015-16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After two years away from the game due to a jail term, Appling returned to basketball for the 2018–19 season, signing with [[Cañeros del Este]] of the Dominican Republic.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Austin|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2018/06/keith_appling_back_in_pro_bask.html|title=Keith Appling back in pro basketball after jail stint|work=[[MLive.com]]|date=June 16, 2018|access-date=June 17, 2018}}</ref> He later joined the [[Abejas de León]] of the Mexican league.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gómez |first=Karla Irene |date=October 22, 2018 |title=Abejas clava el aguijón a los Soles |url=https://www.lavozdelafrontera.com.mx/deportes/abejas-clava-el-aguijon-a-los-soles-2213057.html |access-date=November 4, 2018 |work=La Voz de la Frontera |language=es}}</ref>

He signed with Pallacanestro Piacentina in Italy on March 19, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Keith Appling Signs with Bakery Piacenza |url=https://www.ballersabroad.com/news/keith-appling-signs-with-bakery-piacenza |access-date=March 19, 2019 |work=Ballers Abroad|date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Appling is the son of Tottie Williams and majored in [[sociology]].<ref name=bio/>

===Legal issues===
In July 2017, Appling was sentenced to one year in county jail and four years of probation for carrying a concealed weapon and resisting a police officer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/wayne/2017/07/03/michigan-state-keith-appling-pleads-guilty/448205001/ |last=Anderson |first=Elisha |title=Ex-MSU star Keith Appling to spend a year in jail |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=July 3, 2017|access-date=February 15, 2020}}</ref> In February 2020, Appling was charged with delivery or manufacture of 19 grams of heroin in a car he was attempting to sell.<ref>{{cite news |date=February 15, 2020 |title=Ex-Michigan State star Keith Appling facing heroin charges |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28708436 |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> In May 2021, Appling was arrested for the shooting death of a 66-year-old man in [[Detroit]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Salvador |first=Joseph |date=May 22, 2021 |title=Former Michigan State Basketball Star Keith Appling Wanted in Fatal Shooting |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/05/23/keith-appling-wanted-in-fatal-shooting |access-date=May 23, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> On February 13, 2023, Appling pled guilty to second-degree murder and a firearm charge.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 13, 2023 |title=Former Michigan State star pleads guilty in 2021 murder case |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-crime-indictments-michigan-a8b83b35b1f1bfba8e1c5a23a5112ab4 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |work=AP News}}</ref> On March 3, 2023, Appling was sentenced to eighteen to forty years in prison for the second-degree murder and two years for the firearm charge.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 3, 2023 |title=Former Michigan State guard Appling sentenced in murder case |url=https://apnews.com/article/keith-appling-sentenced-michigan-state-university-8f8b63c4d395b6f0fe35faff213218cb |access-date=March 4, 2023 |work=AP News}}</ref>
